title: Section 135 — Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person

content.overview: BNS s. 135 — Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person. BNS restatement of IPC 357. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 357. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 135 is the rule on “Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person”. The section provides that whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 135 exists so that “Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

enhancement.definition: BNS s. 135 penalizes whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Suppresses attempts to unlawfully deprive individuals of their total physical liberty by criminalizing preparatory violence or threats aimed at confining them.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 135 (corresponding to IPC s. 357).
Actus reus: Assaulting (s. 130) or using criminal force (s. 129).
Specific intent: In attempting wrongfully to confine that person (s. 127).
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to one year, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both (fine modernized from ₹1,000 under IPC 357).
essentialIngredients: The accused assaulted or used criminal force against the victim.
The act was done in an attempt to wrongfully confine the victim within circumscribing boundaries.
The attempt was unlawful and without legal justification.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 135 carries forward IPC 357. It deals with situations where an assailant attempts to force a victim into total confinement (such as dragging someone toward an open cell, forcing someone into a car trunk, or pushing someone into a room to lock the door), but the confinement is not completed because the victim escapes, fights back, or is rescued. While completed wrongful confinement is punished under Section 127, Section 135 penalizes the assault or criminal force used during the attempt itself. The punishment extends up to one year imprisonment, a fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
examples: Teaching example (Attempting to shove into a room): An accused grabs a colleague by the shoulders and tries to force him into a windowless storage closet to lock him in; the colleague breaks free and runs away. The accused is guilty under s. 135.

Teaching example (Attempted car abduction): Assailants tackle a victim on the street and attempt to force him into the back of a van to lock him inside; passersby intervene and pull the victim away. The assailants are liable under s. 135.
distinctions: Section 135 vs Section 127: Section 127 applies to completed wrongful confinement; Section 135 penalizes the assault/force used in the attempt.
Section 135 vs Section 131: Section 131 covers general unprovoked assault (up to 3 months); Section 135 elevates the penalty to 1 year because of the specific intent to confine.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who cornered a shopkeeper, grabbed his hands, and attempted to push him into a basement cellar before neighbors intervened is punishable under s. 135.
Rule: Using criminal force in an attempt to wrongfully confine a person constitutes an offence under BNS s. 135.
Application: Criminal force was used specifically to force the victim into total circumscribed confinement.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 135.

Applies when total confinement is attempted but not completed.
Punishable with up to one year imprisonment, fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
Higher penalty than simple assault due to the gravity of confinement.
